# Cigarette Comparison

An interactive brand ledger at https://dillingerstaffing.github.io/cigarettes/ comparing 53 cigarette brands
across 19 factors in five categories: standardized measurements, product design, smoke chemistry, user behavior,
and user biology.

Core rule of the dataset: FTC machine yields (tar, nicotine, CO, in mg per cigarette) are standardized product
characteristics measured by a smoking machine. They are not human doses. Actual exposure depends on how a person
smokes (puffing, vent blocking, compensation, cigarettes per day, inhalation depth) and on their biology
(nicotine metabolism through CYP2A6, tolerance, preexisting health).

## What the page offers

- A two-brand comparison bench with machine-yield metrics and pack glyphs.
- Three switchable scatterplots of tar, nicotine, and CO across all 53 brands.
- An interactive exposure-workload register (dials for behavior and biology inputs).
- Constituent-to-body pathways for nicotine, tar, and carbon monoxide.
- All 19 factors as expandable entries, each stating what the factor is, what it means, and how it affects the smoker.
- A searchable, sortable atlas of all 53 brands.
- Source links and a JSON download of the full dataset.

## Data limits

53 entries, mostly historical US products. 13 entries lack a sourced measurement year. Sources are global rather
than record-specific. No per-brand disease scores are given; that would require evidence the dataset does not have.
